J1_line_asserts_challenged_proposition.justification: The response challenges the assertion that, given agreement of the ratios on parts of pi ^ sigma, the elements u_i (constant on parts of pi) and v_i (constant on parts of sigma) with u_i v_i = a_i b_i^{-1} can be chosen in exactly |G|^{|pi v sigma|} ways. First-choice line 157 is 'We claim that this can be done in $|G|^{|\pi\vee\sigma|}$ ways, where $|\rho|$ denotes the number of parts of $\rho$', which asserts precisely that count. Active assumptions: lines 135-137 (S_pi, S_sigma), line 152 ('This is zero unless the ratios a_i b_i^{-1} agree on parts of tau = pi ^ sigma'), lines 153-155 (the choice of u constant on pi-parts, v constant on sigma-parts with u_i v_i = a_i b_i^{-1}), and G a finite group with n >= 2 (line 76).

J2_evidence_specified.justification: A complete refuting argument with an explicit configuration: 'For n=4, pi={{1,2},{3,4}}, sigma={{1,4},{2,3}}, and a_i b_i^{-1} = z_i, the system requires u_1 v_1 = z_1, u_1 v_2 = z_2, u_4 v_2 = z_3, and u_4 v_1 = z_4, which implies z_1^{-1} z_2 = z_4^{-1} z_3; there are 0 choices if the z_i do not satisfy this relation.' The four equations are exactly what the constancy conditions force, and the derived obstruction is stated in closed form.

J3_evidence_check.justification: Verified by exhaustive enumeration of the supplied configuration (scripts/P33_check.py). For pi = {{1,2},{3,4}} and sigma = {{1,4},{2,3}}: pi ^ sigma is the partition into singletons, so line 152's precondition ('the ratios agree on parts of tau') is vacuous and every choice of z_1..z_4 is admissible at line 153; and pi v sigma = {{1,2,3,4}}, so line 157 claims exactly |G|^1 = |G| ways. Enumerating all u constant on pi-parts and v constant on sigma-parts: in G = Z/2 with z = (0,1,0,0) (which violates z_1^{-1}z_2 = z_4^{-1}z_3) the number of solutions is 0, not |G| = 2; in G = S_3 with z = (e, (12), e, e) it is 0, not 6. When the derived relation does hold, the count is exactly |G| (2 and 6 respectively), confirming that the response's obstruction is the only failure mode. So the supplied argument refutes line 157 as written. The response left the group and the particular z_i unnamed; I instantiated the two smallest cases to confirm that violating z exist, which is verification of its stated obstruction, not a substitute witness.

J4_consequence_overreach.justification: The response states only that the count can be 0; it makes no claim about the closure of the span (line 131/146), the Theorem at line 216, or the AS-free consequence at line 237.

notes: The obstruction is real and independent of commutativity (it shows up in Z/2 as well as S_3), and it is not screened off by line 152, because for this pi, sigma the meet is the all-singletons partition. A second reader should note the one thing the response leaves implicit: that groups and ratio tuples violating z_1^{-1}z_2 = z_4^{-1}z_3 exist at all (they do in every group of order at least 2, e.g. z = (e, g, e, e) with g non-trivial).
